doc.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Anniversary, staying healthy and goodbyes
summary: The interview ends with their anniversary since 1954, the band's healthy habits and thanks.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Tim, why don’t you flip that? Tim: We’re at almost two hours.
We are at two hours? Oh my God it’s twenty to four. I don’t believe it.
See how you are when you’re having fun?
I can’t believe it.
Both of you all are beautiful.
No I saw the sign and I thought you made a mistake. I can’t believe it. Well, you guys are going to be celebrating your what anniversary now coming up? That’s a real tough question, right?
Let me see. Well since 1954. So that’s 40 and—
Five. Actually 44.
That’s great.
Yeah, we’ve been patting our foot to music.
Music keeps you young.
I think it does.
You can say that again. I’m a strong voucher for that.

And you’ve really got to take care of yourself on the road. See, believe me. And everybody in our new band, they eat grass and seeds. Well Cat Daddy is a professional runner. He’s a champion in his age group. And these guys just don’t drink. They don’t drink, they eat salads and stuff like that.
That’s the truth.
Well this group of guys and you are going to last a long time then I suspect.
Well as long as we keep drinking our gin and eating our steak.
Balance.
Got that balance.
Got to have that balance. Well it’s been a great pleasure for me to talk to you.
Oh, mutually so. Believe me. This has been beautiful.
So I look forward to it, and I hope that your next recording is soon.
We hope so too.
We hope so too. We’re working on it.
And I hope that we can get you out on our end of the country.
I hope we can bring the whole band out so we can really show what the Kansas City style © Fillius Jazz Archive -39-
Well on behalf of Hamilton College, I’d like to thank Jeannie and Jimmy Cheatham for being here today.
And we sure appreciate it.
And I appreciate your — you know we’ve had a balance in this conversation too, you know? Kind of the way up here stuff to think about, and kind of that basic blues stuff to think about too.
Why not?
Well thanks for your time.
Oh you’re welcome. Thank you so much. A real pleasure. © Fillius Jazz Archive -40-
